text: Fixed. In errors.go, `Unwrap()` was declared on `*Error` (pointer receiver), so a plain `Error` value — which is what you passed to `fmt.Errorf("%w", ...)` — did not implement `interface{ Unwrap() error }`. The `%w` verb therefore stored no unwrappable error, and both `errors.Is` and `errors.As` reported "not found". Changed it to a value receiver (`func (msg Error) Unwrap() error`), matching the existing value-receiver `Error()` method, so both `Error` and `*Error` unwrap correctly. Verified: `errors.Is(wrapped, innerErr)` and `errors.As(wrapped, &target)` are now true for the value form, the pointer form still works, and the full `go test ./` suite passes.

Fixed. In response_writer.go, `WriteHeader` warned when headers had already been written but still overwrote `w.status`, so `Status()` reported a code that was never sent. It now returns early after the warning, keeping the status that was actually written (matching the documented "Wanted to override" behavior). Verified with a repro: after `WriteHeader(200)` + `WriteHeaderNow()` + `WriteHeader(401)`, `Status()` is 200 and the recorder still shows 200. Full `go test ./...` passes.
